name: Diff / Patch Application
description: A contributor-authored unified diff (patch_diff) that must apply cleanly (via real `git apply`) to a fixed base file and produce EXACTLY the documented final content -- single-file, conflict-free patch APPLICATION, not merge resolution. The harness always writes base_file_content to one harness-chosen filename ('target.txt') in a fresh workdir; patch_diff is rejected outright if its own diff headers name any other file, or more than one file.
executionEnv: git (git apply, no `git init`/repo needed -- git apply works directly against plain files in a directory)

fields.label: Task description
fields.help: Natural-language description of the change the patch must make, e.g. 'fix the off-by-one error in the loop's upper bound', 'add a null-check before dereferencing the config field', 'rename the data parameter to payload throughout', 'extract the duplicated validation logic into a helper function'.

fields.label: Base file content
fields.help: The original file's full, exact text content, before the patch is applied. Can be any language or plain text -- this category never executes the file's own semantics, only verifies that patch_diff mechanically transforms this exact text into expected_final_content. Written verbatim (no reformatting) to a fixed filename ('target.txt') the harness controls; patch_diff must target that same filename.

fields.label: Patch (unified diff)
fields.help: THE GRADED ARTIFACT. A unified diff / git-style patch (the output of `git diff` against a file named target.txt is the expected shape) that transforms base_file_content into expected_final_content. Header lines MUST read exactly '--- a/target.txt' and '+++ b/target.txt' (git's own default unified-diff header convention) -- any other path, or a patch touching more than one file, is rejected outright before it is ever applied. Must contain at least one real content-changing hunk (a context-only, no-op patch is rejected as a dataset defect).

fields.label: Expected final content
fields.help: The exact file content after patch_diff is applied to base_file_content, compared byte-for-byte (including trailing-newline presence/absence -- unified diffs encode that unambiguously via the standard '\ No newline at end of file' marker, so a correctly authored patch always reproduces it exactly).
